newsitem.title: THAILAND: Planes on standby to evacuate Thais from Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Planes on standby to evacuate Thais from Cambodia.

text.p: The Thai army has three military aircraft on standby to evacuate more than 300 Thais stranded in Cambodia where fighting has escalated between troops loyal to the country's two premiers, army sources said on Sunday.
The army has three C-130 aircraft at a Thai military airport awaiting clearance from Phnom Penh authorities to fly in, the sources told Reuters.

The airport at the Cambodian capital was closed on Saturday and there has been no word on whether any planes would be allowed to land on Sunday. Several commercial airlines said on Saturday that they had cancelled their Sunday flights due to the unstable political situation.
The Red Cross said on Sunday there were 52 casualties from the fighting but gave no breakdown on the number of deaths or injuries. At least four people were reported killed on Friday.
The fighting intensified on Sunday between forces loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Ranariddh, who is in France on what officials said was a family visit, has accused Hun Sen of staging a coup during his absence.
